title: kv: microcompaction + stepped-evictor to reduce fragmentation and spill pressure
author: Aisha Moreno
description:
Motivation: We continue to see tail latency and memory pressure in high-concurrency KV workloads due to small-object fragmentation and episodic spill bursts when many small entries are freed/rewritten. This PR implements two complementary runtime changes: 1) a lightweight background microcompaction that opportunistically coalesces adjacent small free slots into larger free ranges, reducing fragmentation and improving allocator fit behavior; 2) a stepped evictor/pager that applies graduated spillback pressure instead of an immediate all-or-nothing spill when the spill queue grows. Both changes are intended to reduce the frequency and magnitude of on-disk spillover events while keeping P99 latency stable.

Summary of changes (single-line list): - new runtime module src/runtime/kv/microcompact.rs implementing a compact-on-threshold micropass - refactor of evictor into src/runtime/kv/evictor.rs with SteppedEvictor strategy and spill throttling knobs - allocator heuristics: tune slab bin coalescing and introduce per-tenant retention windows - new metrics and telemetry hooks to measure compaction runs, reclaimed_bytes, spill_throttle_events - integration tests and microbench harness: tests/kv/fragmentation_sim.py, bench/kv/microcompact_bench.rs - docs: docs/kv/pager-tuning.md with recommended settings and notes on tradeoffs

Checklist: - [x] Benchmark microbench and internal perf harness (bench results in PR comment) - [x] Unit & integration tests added - [x] Telemetry (metrics + tracing) added - [x] Docs for ops: pager-tuning.md - [x] Reviewed and approved by SRE and runtime leads

Commits (high level): ["a1b2c3d - implement microcompact pass and unit tests","b2c3d4e - implement stepped evictor with throttle state machine","c3d4e5f - expose metrics and tracing spans for compaction","d4e5f6a - perf tune thresholds and add linear ticket references","e5f6a7b - docs: pager tuning and rollout notes"]

Changed areas (high level, small snippets included where helpful): [
  "src/runtime/kv/microcompact.rs - new: lightweight compaction pass that iterates free runs and performs coalesce_if_adjacent(). Snippet: 'if run.length <= micro_threshold { try_coalesce(run) }'",
  "src/runtime/kv/evictor.rs - refactor and new SteppedEvictor state machine (idle -> warn -> throttle -> spill). Snippet: 'match state { State::Warn => increase_backpressure(), State::Throttle => schedule_spill_rate(limit) }'",
  "src/runtime/kv/allocator.rs - adjust slab bin sizing and per-tenant retention windows to avoid hot churn on small objects",
  "bench/kv/microcompact_bench.rs - synthetic workload with 70% small-object churn to validate P99 impact",
  "tests/kv/fragmentation_sim.py - fuzz harness for allocation/free patterns, asserts on reclaimed bytes and spill counts",
  "docs/kv/pager-tuning.md - ops guidance and recommended defaults for steady vs bursty workloads"
]

Design notes and rationale: The microcompactor is intentionally conservative: it runs on a dedicated low-priority executor and limits compaction work by reclaimed-bytes-per-second so it does not interfere with latency-sensitive token generation. The stepped evictor introduces an intermediate 'throttle' level where we slow down incoming allocation admission and rate-limit background spill threads rather than immediately launching large spill jobs. This reduces IO bursts and results in smaller, more frequent spill batches which our benchmarks indicate yields lower tail latency and better average throughput for mixed-size requests.

Benchmarks (summary): Using bench harness with 200 concurrent connections and a 70% small-write churn workload, we observed: - 18% reduction in mean mem-usage under steady load - 34% reduction in spill bytes during short bursts (2-10s) - 12% improvement in P99 latency for KV-heavy paths (end-to-end generation unaffected) Full bench log attached in comment 'bench-log-88766.txt'.

Review conversation (high level): - Jonah Li (reviewer): "Can the microcompaction lead to pathological CPU usage under sustained free churn?" - Aisha (author): "We cap compactor work to 50MB/s by default and it yields negligible CPU in our perf runs; added metric runtime.kv.microcompact.cpu_ms to monitor." - Priya Suresh: "Need clear ops knobs per cluster (steady vs bursty); recommend adding a chart and default override per-pool." - Aisha: "Added docs/kv/pager-tuning.md with per-pool recommendations and a Grafana dashboard template." - Marco D'Angelo: "Please sanity-check cross-tenant fairness when retention windows are enabled." - Aisha: "Retention windows are tenant-scoped and opt-in; added tests to ensure tenant A's compaction does not bump tenant B's eviction priority."

CI notes: One flaky test (kv::integration::evictor_race) failed on first run due to a test harness timing assumption; test was made resilient and CI re-ran. Final CI status: all checks passed; new metrics compilation warnings fixed.

Rollout and ops: This change is behind two feature flags: runtime.kv.microcompact.enabled (default: on) and runtime.kv.evictor.stepped_enabled (default: on for dedicated and private; off for hosted until staged rollout). Ops should watch metrics: runtime.kv.reclaimed_bytes, runtime.kv.spill_throttle_events, runtime.kv.spill_bytes, and runtime.kv.microcompact.cpu_ms. Docs include recommended defaults and a migration path for clusters with very large slab sizes.

Merge: Squash-merged to main. Migration notes included in docs/kv/pager-tuning.md.
